charts.name: Siting screen
charts.display_name: Operators that added 150 MW+ of baseload · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: Status: Act when cutting the peak 10% needs over 10 hours of storage or the data doesn't reconcile (closure outside ±2%); Watch when it needs 4–10 hours, batteries cover under half the bad-day ramp, or baseload rose beyond weather (proven); Good otherwise.

charts.name: Evening ramp, median day
charts.subtitle: Median day · Jul–Sep 2026
charts.description: The largest 3-hour rise in net load after the solar peak, median day of the quarter. Compared only where 9 days in 10 had a duck in both years.

charts.name: Evening ramp, bad day
charts.subtitle: 1 day in 10 · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: The evening ramp on 1 day in 10 (P90) over 12 months: what storage is sized to.

charts.name: Hours to cut the peak
charts.subtitle: Of storage · 1 day in 10 · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: Hours of storage to cut the daily net-load peak by 10% on 1 day in 10. Within 4 h a 4-hour battery covers it; over 10 h needs long-duration storage.

charts.name: Baseload
charts.subtitle: 5th percentile of demand · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: The 5th percentile of hourly demand, a proxy for flat load.

charts.name: Net load by hour and month
charts.display_name: Net load by hour and month, MW · last 24 months
charts.description: Mean net load by hour of day and month. Darker is more to serve; the evening ramp is the climb from the midday trough to the evening peak.

charts.name: Daily evening ramps by month
charts.display_name: Daily evening ramp, GW · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: Every day's evening ramp, one box per month: the box is the middle half, the whiskers the 10th and 90th percentile days. Storage is sized to the upper whisker.

charts.name: Evening ramp bridge
charts.display_name: What moved the mean day's evening ramp, GW · Jul–Sep 2025 to Jul–Sep 2026
charts.description: The change in the mean day's evening ramp split exactly into demand, solar and wind: each step is how much that source's swing across the day's 3-hour window changed.

charts.name: Evening ramp by operator
charts.display_name: Ten largest evening ramps, GW · Jul–Sep 2026
charts.description: Operators with a duck (solar a tenth of midday demand): the evening ramp on the median day and on 1 day in 10. A rising ramp is amber, a falling one green.

charts.name: Is the change real
charts.display_name: Evening ramp: each month's change ÷ weather noise

metrics: SQL(MAX(CASE WHEN outside_noise_band THEN z_noise END)) AS Outside the band
SQL(MAX(CASE WHEN NOT outside_noise_band THEN z_noise END)) AS Inside the band
SQL(MAX(CASE WHEN n_z_12m = 12 THEN z_mean_12m END)) AS 12-month average

charts.description: Each month's year-on-year change divided by this operator's own weather noise for that month. Outside the band three months running, or a 12-month average above the dashed line, counts as real. Tested only with four reference years of a duck.

charts.name: Is it real, by operator
charts.display_name: Verdict by operator · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: Proven: the 12-month test passed (beyond what weather produces 1 time in 100). Watch: outside the weather band three months running. Every operator with a proven or watched rise on any test.

charts.name: Evening ramp since 2018
charts.display_name: Evening ramp, GW · median and bad day, by month since Jul 2018
charts.description: Months when solar was under 5% of peak demand have no evening ramp and are left blank.

charts.name: Baseload and peak added by grid operator
charts.display_name: ◇ Baseload and peak added, MW · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: Baseload is the 5th percentile of hourly demand, peak the 95th. Where they rise together the new load is flat; peak also moves with summer weather.

charts.name: Baseload against 2019
charts.description: Each operator's baseload against its own 2019, coloured by whether its rise passes the 12-month test.

charts.name: Load-zone baseload since 2019
charts.display_name: PJM load zones: ◇ baseload, 2019 = 100 · trailing 12 months
charts.description: Dominion's Virginia zone (DOM) and American Electric Power's (AEP): lowest hours at night, so their 5th percentile is flat load.

charts.name: Operators covered
charts.display_name: Operators whose batteries cover the ramp
charts.subtitle: Battery MW ≥ the bad-day ramp · of 51

charts.name: Operators within 4 hours
charts.subtitle: Cut the peak 10% in 4 h or less · of 51

charts.name: Batteries installed by region
charts.display_name: Batteries operating by region, GW · EIA-860M, August 2026

charts.name: Battery cover of the bad-day ramp
charts.display_name: ◇ Battery MW ÷ bad-day evening ramp · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: Operating battery nameplate MW over the bad-day (P90) evening ramp, for operators whose bad-day ramp is 1 GW or more. Nameplate isn't accredited capacity.

charts.name: Hours of storage to cut the peak
charts.display_name: ◇ Hours of storage to cut the peak 10% · 1 day in 10 · 12 months to Sep 2026
charts.description: The energy above 90% of the day's peak net load divided by that 10%, on 1 day in 10: perfect foresight, no losses. Operators with a peak over 5 GW.

charts.name: What serves 13:00 and 20:00
charts.description: Mean supply by fuel at 13:00, when solar peaks, and 20:00, after it sets. Below zero is where part of it goes, exports and battery charging, so each bar nets to demand. Months whose generation is more than 5% off demand are left out.

charts.name: Battery output by hour
charts.display_name: Battery discharge by hour, MW · Jul–Sep 2026 vs Jul–Sep 2025
charts.description: Discharge only: EIA-930 reports some operators' batteries net of charging and others as discharge only (ERCOT switched in Dec 2025).

charts.name: Solar at 13:00
charts.metric: SQL(SUM(CASE WHEN fuel_group = 'Solar' AND hour_label = '13:00' THEN mean_mw END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN hour_label = '13:00' AND mean_mw > 0 THEN mean_mw END), 0)) AS Solar at 13:00
charts.subtitle: Of supply at that hour · Jul–Sep 2026

charts.name: Gas at 20:00
charts.metric: SQL(SUM(CASE WHEN fuel_group = 'Gas' AND hour_label = '20:00' THEN mean_mw END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN hour_label = '20:00' AND mean_mw > 0 THEN mean_mw END), 0)) AS Gas at 20:00
charts.subtitle: Of supply at that hour · Jul–Sep 2026

charts.name: Balance closure
charts.subtitle: Jul–Sep 2026 · ±2% guardrail
charts.description: (Net generation − interchange − demand) ÷ demand. Green within ±2%; red outside, where fuel shares are approximate. Beyond ±5% the fuel mix is left blank.

charts.name: Glossary
charts.display_name: Glossary · every measure on the dashboard

charts.name: Data quality by grid operator
charts.display_name: Operators with a month past ±2% closure · latest 12 months
charts.description: Balance closure is (net generation − interchange − demand) ÷ demand and should sit near zero. Red rows: six or more months past ±2%; amber: one to five.

charts.name: CAISO balance closure
charts.display_name: Balance closure by month, % · CAISO and PJM · since Jan 2024
charts.description: CAISO's fuel mix stops reconciling from Dec 2025 (its ramp uses only demand, solar and wind and is unaffected); PJM runs above +2% each summer.
